text:
Added tools/disposable-slurm/capture-squeue-absence.sh, which automates the whole capture: builds the pinned Slurm image, starts the controller, holds a real array job in the queue, runs squeue for (unknown-only, mixed, queued-only), and writes raw stdout/stderr/exit plus a provenance.json with sizes and SHA-256 digests. It needs a controller only -- no worker registration, no job execution -- because an unknown job id yields the same diagnostic either way, which is what makes this reproducible on a laptop instead of blocked on a site allocation.

The decisive artifact is mixed.stdout: non-empty means squeue returns surviving queue state alongside the diagnostic; empty means it refuses the whole query and only single-job absence is knowable. SlurmCliScheduler is already correct under either answer (it claims absence only for jobs the response accounts for), so this capture confirms rather than unblocks.

NOT YET RUN OR SYNTAX-CHECKED: Docker Desktop would not start on the review machine (daemon unreachable after ~72s), and shell execution was declined, so the script has not been executed or even parsed. Treat it as unverified until someone runs it.
